architecture: internal/engine/engine.go:1-4,263-300 — the engine package runs the full pipeline (parser.Parse, then analyze, plan and open a cursor). Protocol and server sit on top of it; storage/pqcf/index sit below it

Package import graph (non-test): sql/lexer imports only errs, sql/parser imports only lexer/ast/errs, storage imports only errs/types, optimizer imports only plan/types. Layers are acyclic and only point downward. Small leak: protocol imports exec directly as well as engine

internal/optimizer/optimizer.go:1-60 — a logical optimizer of named Rule implementations (ConstantFolding, PredicatePushdown, JoinReorder, ColumnPruning), one file each. Physical choices (access path, join algorithm, execution mode, native kernels) are kept separate in package physical

internal/errs/*.go:1-80 — one structured error model with stable spec codes and SQL line/column details, shared by every layer. internal/native is isolated behind a cgo/stub build split (native_cgo.go / native_stub.go)
readability: internal/sql/parser/parser.go:98-933 — textbook recursive descent with one small function per grammar level (orExpr, andExpr, predicate, additive, ...) and consistent errs.At position errors

internal/exec/vagg.go:15-50 — a block comment explains why the design was chosen (batch group-ID resolution, struct-of-arrays states, mergeable states for parallel workers). The aggState interface methods are documented

Function size is mostly moderate, but a few run over 100 lines: analyzer/query.go:53 selectBlock (~136), exec/subquery.go:80 compileSubquery (~131), exec/functions.go:15 compileFunc (~131), exec/build.go:33 build (~119)
Large files in exec (vexpr.go 1113 lines, vagg.go 1240, vsort.go 698), and cmd/polyquery/main.go:66-74 reads an undocumented POLYQUERY_MORSEL_ROWS test-only env var inside production arg parsing
robustness: internal/protocol/handler.go:118-135 — guard() turns errors into coded responses and recovers panics into INTERNAL_ERROR with a logged stack. server/server.go:621-628 and server/stream.go:126-130 do the same for streamed queries

internal/engine/engine.go:157-201 — request paths are checked (absolute paths, '..' and NUL are rejected with ACCESS_DENIED). File size is checked by stat and again by LimitReader against MaxIngestBytes, and OS errors map to NOT_FOUND/ACCESS_DENIED/IO_ERROR

internal/pqcf/read.go:95-160 — PQCF parsing checks size, magic, version (UNSUPPORTED vs CORRUPT), flags, metadata length bounds, CRC, UTF-8, required keys, negative row_count and the max-rows limit before trusting anything

Gaps: worker goroutines in exec/parallel.go:249 and :530 (and vagg.go:1081/1096, vsort.go:402/427) have no recover, so a panic in a worker kills the process instead of reaching guard(). The parser has no nesting-depth limit (parser.go:525-733), so deeply nested SQL can overflow the stack. protocol/session.go:16 ReadBytes has no line-length cap. native.go:124-127 panics on short buffers (an internal invariant)
testability: 114 Test functions across 23 _test.go files (~4050 lines vs ~26.8k source), covering types, parser, analyzer, optimizer, physical, exec, storage, pqcf, index, ingest, catalog, protocol, server and native
internal/testutil/testutil.go:1-40 — a shared fixture catalog (emp/dept from inline CSV) makes pipeline-level unit tests cheap to write
internal/optimizer/optimizer_test.go:20-60 — each rule can be tested on its own through the Rule interface. Helpers check that rules do not mutate their input plan and assert on the printed plan text

Gaps: no dedicated tests for sql/lexer (only reached through the parser) or errs. No Fuzz targets for the parser, protocol decoding or the PQCF reader, which handle untrusted input. engine/bench_test.go has only benchmarks

top_strengths: Clean, acyclic layering (lexer → parser → analyzer → logical plan → rule optimizer → physical planner → row/vectorized exec → storage/pqcf), with each optimizer rule in its own file
Consistent structured error model (errs.Code with SQL positions) carried end to end, plus panic-to-INTERNAL_ERROR guards at the protocol and HTTP boundaries
Defensive handling of untrusted input: path-traversal checks, ingest size limits, a memory-reservation budget, and strict PQCF header/metadata/CRC validation
Idiomatic Go with doc comments that explain design reasons, and a test-fixture package that makes component tests cheap to add
top_weaknesses: Panics inside parallel worker goroutines (exec/parallel.go:249,530; vagg.go; vsort.go) are not recovered and would crash the whole server or session process
No recursion-depth limit in the recursive-descent parser or analyzer, and no line-length cap on JSON-lines session input
Several 100+ line functions and 1000+ line files in exec and analyzer make the vectorized and subquery paths harder to follow
No fuzz tests for the parser, protocol or PQCF reader, and no direct lexer unit tests
